conditions: The message is posted in the channel #incidents.
The message's content concerns a payment gateway outage.
Diego Alvarez has added a fire-emoji reaction to that same message.
A rocket-emoji reaction is added to that same message (by the requesting bot).

readings: Presupposes there is exactly one message in #incidents about a payment gateway outage, identified independently of the fire-reaction clause
Relies on the combination with 'that Diego Alvarez reacted to with fire' to pick out a unique message among possibly several payment-gateway-outage messages
Any custom emoji whose name/appearance evokes fire (e.g. :dumpster_fire:, :on_fire:)
A single, uniquely identifiable workspace user with this exact name
Possibly ambiguous if multiple users share this name or a similar display name

turn2.differences: The author's c1-c3 map directly onto my step-1 conditions 1-3 (channel, topic, Diego's fire reaction). The action itself (adding the rocket reaction) is correctly treated as the task to perform rather than a filter condition, which matches my reading. No discrepancies.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Multiple messages in #incidents concern the payment gateway outage (.000001, .000002, .000003, .000004, .000006), so the phrase alone isn't unique. But combined with the fire-reaction-by-Diego clause, exactly one message (.000001) satisfies both, so the two possible readings converge on the same result here — the ambiguity doesn't actually create uncertainty in this dataset.
All reactions in the data use the plain type 'fire' with no custom fire-themed emoji present, so there's no real alternate reading to consider for this record set.
Only one user (U_DIEGO, real_name 'Diego Alvarez') exists in the workspace, so there is no competing candidate for the name.
